fields.summary: Improve messaging experience for users who do not have permission to reply

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

fields.description:
It is possible for a user to receive a message that they do not have permission to reply to, for example a teacher/admin may have the capability to message a student who does not have the capability to send messages. There is already handling in the backend to prevent the student in this example from sending a message, but there is no indication in the UI until they try to send a message:

!sending_rejected_error.png|width=200,height=183!

This is not a great experience because (a) the message is not very user friendly (using IDs etc), and (b) the timing of the message means the student would have to first write an entire message and hit send to see it, which is a frustrating experience that costs them unnecessary time.

The purpose of this issue is to make it more obvious in the UI _before_ the user tries to send a message. I would propose these requirements:

# Update the error message string so that it is more user friendly. We can probably make it more generic, for example "You do not have permission to send messages in this conversation".
# Persistently display the language string at the bottom of conversations the user cannot reply in, using the same elements currently displaying the error after they try to send the message. This should preemptively make it obvious to the user that they will not be able to reply to the message.
# If possible, disable the messaging textarea and/or send button, so it is really obvious to the user that they cannot send a message.
# We must retain the existing backend error functionality in addition to the above, particularly for security reasons, so that if someone trying to bypass the UI (eg sending directly via web service) that still receives an error response and the message is not sent.

I believe that the messaging textarea is common across all conversations, and it is possible that the user may be able to message some users and not others, so we will need to investigate whether that situation is possible (eg contacts vs non contacts), and if so, if it is possible to check whether the user is allowed to send in a conversation when that conversation is loaded, and if they don't have the access, disable the relevant form elements (and if they are allowed, make sure we re-enable the the elements so they can send messages in those cases). It also means we should not clear the text area when we disable or enable it, because the text carries between conversations and we don't want them to lose what they've written somewhere else if they flick between conversations.

components.name: JavaScript

fields.description:
At least one JavaScript component or functionality is not compatible with accessibility technologies. For example : 

* The ARIA Menubar design pattern is not relevant on the main menu.  
* The aria-expanded property is not relevant to the "Close" button on the search engine.  
* The aria-haspopup property is not relevant on the "Display notification window without new notification" button.
* The aria-expanded property is not relevant to the "Notification Window" region. 
*  The messaging component is a "show/hide" zone which does not respect the principles of the ARIA Disclosure design pattern.  
* In messaging, on a conversation, the "..." button which displays additional actions has no name.  - In messaging, on a conversation, the "Enable/disable emoji selector" component manages a "show/hide" zone which does not respect the principles of the ARIA Disclosure design pattern.  - The "Remove conversation from favourites" and "Delete conversation" components trigger JavaScript events, but are implemented in links.  - The accessible name of the "User menu" button, given by its aria-label property, does not include the initials that are displayed.

* In the user menu, the role="menuitem" elements are not direct descendants of the role="menu" element. 
* The "Previous month" and "Next month" calendar components trigger JavaScript events, but are implemented in links.

Corrections proposal  : 

*  Remove references to the ARIA Menubar design pattern from the main menu.
* Remove the aria-expanded property from the "Close" button in the search engine.
* Remove the aria-haspopup property from the "Display notification window without new notification" button. - Remove the aria-expanded property from the "Notification window" region.
* Implement the ARIA Disclosure design pattern on the "Open/close message drawer" and "Enable/disable emoji selector" buttons: Disclosure (Show/Hide) Pattern
* Modify the aria-label property of the "User menu" button so that it matches the initials displayed.
* In the user menu, add role="none" to the <ul> and <li> elements.
* Implement the "Previous month" and "Next month" buttons in <button> elements.

fields.summary: Add support for Symfony/Console for CLI Commands

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

fields.description:
h2. Summary

Moodle's existing CLI support is based on a custom framework which has evolved over time and requires a significant amount of boilerplate to create and maintain commands.

This issue proposes adding support for the Symfony Console component as a modern framework for new core CLI commands. Symfony Console provides structured command definitions, argument and option handling, automatic help generation, improved output formatting, testing support, and a more consistent developer experience for creating command-line tools.

h2. Initial Scope

The initial implementation will:

* Add the Symfony Console dependency.
* Introduce a new {{bin/moodle}} entry point.
* Provide the infrastructure required to discover, register, and execute Symfony Console commands.
* Support command discovery using Moodle's existing namespace and class conventions.
* Provide standard global runtime options such as {{--showsql}} and {{--showdebugging}}.
* Include developer documentation describing how new commands are created, registered, and executed.

Symfony Console commands introduced by this issue may assume a configured Moodle installation and bootstrap Moodle through {{config.php}}.

h2. Existing CLI Scripts

Existing CLI scripts remain fully supported.

This issue does not seek to replace or remove the existing CLI framework. Existing scripts in {{admin/cli}} should continue to function as they do today.

Where equivalent Symfony Console commands are introduced, they should exist alongside the existing CLI scripts rather than replacing them.

h2. Proof of Concept

The proof of concept should demonstrate both the framework and a realistic command implementation.

This may include:

* Existing functionality exposed through Symfony Console commands (for example, cron-related commands).
* A modernised implementation of functionality currently provided by {{admin/cli/uninstall_plugins.php}}.

Rather than performing a direct one-to-one port of {{uninstall_plugins.php}}, the Symfony Console implementation should demonstrate a more focused command structure.

Examples may include:

{noformat}php bin/moodle plugins:list
php bin/moodle plugins:list --contrib
php bin/moodle plugins:list --missing

php bin/moodle plugins:uninstall mod_assign mod_forum
php bin/moodle plugins:uninstall mod_assign mod_forum --execute

php bin/moodle plugins:purge-missing
php bin/moodle plugins:purge-missing --execute
{noformat}

The existing {{admin/cli/uninstall_plugins.php}} script will remain available and unchanged.

h2. Out of Scope

The following are explicitly out of scope for the first iteration:

* Removal of existing CLI scripts.
* Migration of all existing CLI functionality.
* Plugin-provided Symfony Console commands.
* Installation and pre-installation commands that must operate without a configured Moodle site.
* Replacement of Moodle's existing CLI framework.

h2. Success Criteria

This issue will be considered complete when:

* Symfony Console is available in Moodle through Composer.
* The {{bin/moodle}} entry point can discover and execute Symfony Console commands.
* Commands can be registered using Moodle's standard namespace conventions.
* Proof-of-concept commands have been implemented.
* Developer documentation has been written.

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)

fields.description:
Phase 1 of the Double Marking project.

*AIMED RELEASE:* 5.1 / 5.2

*MAIN FUNCTIONALITY:* ”Double Marking with Marker allocation - joint feedback, separate grade, manual feedback agreement”

----

Phase 1 of the Double Marking project introduces the ability for multiple markers to be allocated to a student’s assignment submission, where they can set individual marks to be calculated into a final grade, via various methods.



Currently, the terms “grade” and “mark” are used somewhat interchangeably in Moodle. This project introduces a clear distinction between the two.

*grade* - is still as it was, the overall final value for an assignment

*mark* - is a separate value set by a “marker”. Think of it as a “provisional grade”.



There can be between 1 and 5 markers allocated to a student submission.

Where you have more than 1 marker, the following options exist for calculation of final grade:

* manual - No automatic calculation. Someone must manually review the marks and choose the final grade.
* first - In this case, the first mark added will be chosen as the final grade
* max - In this case the highest mark added will be chosen as the final grade
* average - In this case an average of the marks added will be chosen. This option has further options to choose how the average is calculated: round up, round down, natural rounding, no rounding



An example workflow for an assignment with 2 allocated markers:

* Assignment created by a teacher, with settings (markingallocation=yes, markingworkflow=yes, markercount=2, multimarkingmethod=max)
* A teacher/manager with “manageallocations” capability can set which teachers are allocated to which students, either on a case-by-case basis using Quick Grading page, Advanced Grader window, or the Bulk Allocate Markers page. E.g. Teacher 1 and Teacher 2 allocated.
* Teacher 1 uses the Quick Grading page and sets a mark of “45” for Student 1
* Teacher 2 uses the Advanced Grader page and sets a mark of “99” for Student 1
* Automatic calculation is run using method “max” and “99” is chosen and set for Student 1’s grade



As well as marks, the workflow state can also be set by the allocated markers and calculated automatically.

The logic for this is:

* If ALL markers have set their mark state to “Marking Complete” then the overall grade workflow state is set to “Marking Complete”.
* If ANY marker has set their mark to anything higher than “Not Marked”, e.g. “In Marking” or “Marking Complete”, then the overall grade workflow is set to “In marking”
* ELSE it is set to “Not Marked”



As well as individual assignments, this also supports Group/Team submissions, in the following way:

* Markers can either be allocated to every student in the group (probably most common) or they can only be assigned to some members of the group
* Marks and workflow states can be set on specific users via the Quick Grading page, like grades can be currently
* Marks and workflow states can be applied to the entire group via the Advanced Marker page, like grades can be currently. However, in this case, they are only applied if the marker is allocated to the student in the group.



Feedback can be left by all markers, however it is currently just in 1 text area and not split into different sections per marker. That is for a later phase of the project.

The new functionality works for Simple grading, such as point or scale, but not for rubrics or marking guides. They will be investigated in a later phase of the project.



*Notes*

* If a user wants to use the functionality how it used to be (currently is, prior to this being integrated), they can set a marker count of 1. They will then still be able to set individual marks and individual workflows, but they don’t have to use them, they can just set the grade and the overall workflow state and ignore the marking option.

Since Moodle 3.5 ([MDL-59159|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-59159]), these rules apply to decide the Minimum PHP and Moodle versions supported:

# An LTS will always require the previous LTS (or later) for upgrading.
# The maximum PHP version supported for a branch will be the maximum one achieved throughout the life of the branch. Usually with .0 releases, but it may happen later (we added support for php70 with 3.0.1 or support for php73 with 3.6.4, for example).
# The minimum PHP version supported for a branch will be *the lower of*:
#* The [minimum version supported in any way by php|http://php.net/supported-versions.php] that is under support for at least 12 more months when the new Moodle version gets released (so we provide slow, progressive increments).
#* The maximum PHP version supported by the previous LTS branch (so we guarantee jumping between LTS is possible without upgrading PHP at the same time).
{panel}

fields.description:
Placements don’t determine the launch container for links. Tools control this via their config (see ”Default launch container” in the configuration form).

When placing a link, a placement should have access to the relevant information about the expected launch mode so it can make decisions about how to present the link (whether that may be an <a> tag, or embedded HTML, or otherwise). 

For example, in the mod_lti case, it is essential to know what the whether the tool is configured to launch links in a new window. This knowledge allows mod_lti to create the link with a relevant onclick handler in the lti_get_coursemodule_info() callback, meaning a user clicking the activity name will instantly be taken to a new window launch of the tool. If the tool isn’t configured for new window launches, then we don’t want this onclick handler. 

I think it’ll be useful to ask core_ltix for the launch container for a _link_, rather than for a _tool_, however (at least in terms of how we express this in an API method name). Calling something like foo::get_launch_container__for_link_() allows greater flexibility in future if/when we decide to let links control their desired launch mode/presentation mode (per the value returned during deep linking). Right now, we can certainly just delegate to the tool’s configuration within such a method.

So, what we’d like to do:

# Create the above API in a sensible place
## This should currently just lookup the tool’s default launch container
# Tests for the above, which really just consists of creating a link for a mock placement of a tool, then checking that we get back the value currently configured on the tool.

fields.summary: Improve select all in course bulk editing

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

fields.description:
The current “Select all” checkbox in the course bulk editing is confusing and, in most cases, unusable.

The main problem is that the same element is used for selecting activities and sections, but before the user selects something, there is no way the component can know what to choose, and it is disabled.

This issue will change the element with a drop-down menu that the user could use to define what to select. The approach is similar to what Gmail does and has already been validated by the UX team.
